clue.text: Politician put in a skirt length reforming order

indicators.note: the politician is placed inside the rearranged letters
reforming means shaping the letters of a skirt length anew

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, stands for a politician

explanation.surface: An MP gets involved in a reform movement over the length of skirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command but is a religious order; 'reforming' rearranges A SKIRT LENGTH, and 'put in' sets the politician inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Knights Templar were a medieval military religious order of crusading monks.

clue.text: Family of gent tangling with amour — farewell Romeo!

indicators.note: tangling with means the letters of gent get mixed up among the other letters
farewell means saying goodbye to a letter, so it is dropped from amour

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A gentleman embroiled in a love affair says goodbye to his Romeo days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'farewell Romeo' drops R from AMOUR to leave AMOU; 'tangling with' mixes GENT and AMOU into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Montagues are Romeo's household in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet, feuding with the Capulets, so a family name.

clue.text: Island language

definitions.meaning: an Indonesian island, home to Jakarta
a widely used computer programming language

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: the Indonesian island and the programming language named after its coffee.

clue.text: Family tree's first thing to be filled by brewer?

definitions.text: thing to be filled by brewer?

indicators.note: first says the tree comes before the family in the answer

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone researching their family tree asks what came first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Family tree' as genealogy; split them: the tree goes first, then the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cask, a quarter of a barrel, which a brewer fills with beer.

clue.text: In good nick? Excellent

parts.note: top as an adjective means best or very good
a notch is a small cut or nick

explanation.surface: Is something in good condition? Then it is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In good nick' is British slang for in good condition, but here it splits into a good word and a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an idiom for of the highest quality, first-rate.

clue.text: Face bit cold? Answer's fur

parts.note: the chin is a part of the face
chill means coldness

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold chin asks what to wear and is told: fur.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent, prized as a luxury fur.

clue.text: Drop everything — last of oil's gone, affecting us all

parts.note: a glob is a drop or blob of liquid

indicators.note: gone means that letter is taken away from everything

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word oil

explanation.surface: When the last drop of oil is gone, it will affect everyone worldwide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' removes L, the 'last of oil', from ALL to leave AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something global is worldwide, touching everyone on the planet.

clue.text: Extremist in a zone that's been torn apart

indicators.note: torn apart means the letters are ripped up and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A militant is spotted in a war zone that has been devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-Nazi is a far-right extremist reviving Nazi ideology.

clue.text: Leaving bedroom in whorehouse, look for Shakespearian character

indicators.note: leaving means the bedroom abbreviation walks out of the word for whorehouse

parts.note: a brothel is a whorehouse
BR is the estate-agent abbreviation for bedroom
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A man leaves a bedroom in a brothel and looks for a character from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' takes BR out of BROTHEL, leaving OTHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moorish general and title role of Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Seeking Dracula as he may be found by day?

definitions.meaning: hunting for Count Dracula, the vampire nobleman

definitions.text: as he may be found by day?
definitions.meaning: a vampire sleeps through daylight, unconscious like a boxer knocked down for ten seconds

explanation.definitionFit: Literally hunting the Count; idiomatically unconscious or fast asleep, as a boxer counted out is.

clue.text: Recover two-year old sheep?

definitions.meaning: a teg is a sheep in its second year; the question mark signals that the first word turned back to front spells it

explanation.surface: A farmer wants to recover a lost young sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: put GET back to front and you have TEG, a two-year-old sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something back is to regain or retrieve it.

clue.text: Small remote-controlled gadget on boat goes wrong when navy intervenes

indicators.note: intervenes means the navy letter comes between the others
goes wrong means the letters of on boat fall out of order

explanation.surface: A remote-controlled device on a boat malfunctions, so the navy steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges ON BOAT; 'intervenes' puts N into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanobot is a microscopic robot, a tiny machine steered remotely.

clue.text: Drunken idiot rumoured to be close

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: rumoured means passed by word of mouth, so we take the spoken form

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A drunk fool is said to be nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is a close one, bound by strong ties.

clue.text: Assesses pros and cons of what cowcatcher does

definitions.meaning: a cowcatcher on a locomotive's front scoops up livestock from the track

explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, reviewing a position; literally, a cowcatcher grabbing cattle, which farmers call stock.

clue.text: Good day when Tigers fail to score?

parts.note: the Tigers is the nickname of Hull City football club
nil or zero is the letter O

explanation.surface: A football fan asks whether it is a good day when the Tigers draw a blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull City, an English football club from the city of Hull, are known as the Tigers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hullo is a greeting, said in the same spirit as a cheery good day.

clue.text: He hit my skittles all over the place — there's no stopping them!

indicators.note: all over the place means the letters are scattered like skittles and fall in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bowler cheers as the ball sends skittles flying, unstoppable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means there is no upper bound on what can be achieved.

clue.text: Supporter of cuts has worse alternative

indicators.note: an alternative is another version, so these letters take another order

explanation.surface: Someone backing spending cuts is told the alternative would be worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of cuts' sounds like politics, but it is a frame supporting wood being sawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawhorse is a trestle that holds timber while a carpenter saws it.

clue.text: Heading north from Austria, I am carrying pine tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

indicators.note: carrying means I am holds the pine word inside it

parts.note: taken as written
to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A traveller heads north from Austria carrying a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A then I(LONG)AM gives AILONGAM, which 'Heading north' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Customs finding precious metal concealed in papers

indicators.note: concealed in means the metal sits hidden inside the papers

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscripts, that is papers
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Customs officers find gold hidden among documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests the border officials of the surface, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and conventions of a community.

clue.text: Live right on eastern part of city?

parts.note: a side is a district, as in New York's East Side

explanation.surface: Someone lives right on the eastern side of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell or have one's home somewhere.

clue.text: I say, what's the reason for hanging around, fisheye?

indicators.note: I say signals that we take the words as spoken rather than written

parts.words: what's the reason for hanging around
parts.note: why asks for the reason; to dangle is to hang loosely or loiter

explanation.surface: Someone asks a loiterer why they are lingering, with a fishy stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisheye is an extreme type of wide-angle camera lens.

clue.text: Department has extreme highs and lows

indicators.note: extreme picks the outer letters at each end of the word highs

explanation.surface: A department has its ups and downs.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths are the lowest points, as in the depths of despair.

clue.text: Country hotels restored with love

indicators.note: restored means the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A nation has its hotels lovingly renovated.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountain kingdom wholly surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Instrument for body running tests in VW

indicators.note: in means the body sits inside the car

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car model
the ICC, International Cricket Council, governs Test cricket

explanation.surface: A car body undergoes tests in a Volkswagen factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are international cricket games, run by the ICC.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small high-pitched flute.

clue.text: Shed players

definitions.meaning: threw off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to throw off or discard; a cast is the company of performers in a production.

clue.text: With reference to fees, Conservative introduced cuts

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to

indicators.note: introduced means the Conservative letter is put inside the fees

parts.note: dues are fees paid for membership

explanation.surface: A Conservative government brings in cuts to fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduces and cuts are synonyms as verbs meaning lowers or diminishes.

clue.text: "Man's woman" stuff

parts.note: he's, a contraction of he is, read as man is
Sian is a Welsh woman's name

explanation.surface: A man's wife is treated as his property.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is coarse sacking cloth; stuff is an old word for woven fabric or material.
